A1.justification: Both complete, readable 21-page PDFs describe the same HSACC research, including the method, experiments, checklist, and Appendix A.1. Text, equations, tables, and figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original clustering results, loss ablations, sensitivity and convergence analyses, multi-view scalability experiments, and main-text and appendix visualizations.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical studies, including the appendix visualizations, and reports revised Noisy MNIST results in Table 1.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same autoencoders, mutual-information alignment, MMD-based weighting and alignment, cross-view inference MLPs, four-loss objective, and final k-means procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate LandUse_21, Noisy MNIST, Caltech101-20, Hdigit, and 100leaves, plus Mfeat with two to five views. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same nine comparators: RPCIC, MRL_CAL, ICMVC, MCAC, PROLMP, DCP, DSIMVC, SURE, and COMP. Revised comparator scores do not change comparator membership.

E3.justification: The reported settings remain identical, including missing rates 0.3/0.5/0.7, ACC/NMI/ARI metrics, network configurations, learning rate, batch size, and training schedule. No protocol revision accompanies the changed Table 1 values.

E4.justification: The loss-combination ablations in Table 2, parameter sensitivity in Figure 2, convergence curves in Figure 4, Mfeat scalability analysis, and t-SNE analyses in Figures 3 and 5 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version adds repeated-run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Both retain the checklist's explicit statement that statistical significance is not reported.

E6.justification: Table 1 substantially revises MCAC and SURE on Noisy MNIST at all three missing rates, and HSACC at 0.5. For example, SURE's ACC at 0.7 changes from 17.93 to 83.12. HSACC's ACC/NMI/ARI at 0.5 changes from 91.37/85.70/83.52 to 92.55/85.92/85.50. The best competing ACC there changes from ICMVC's 86.84 to SURE's 92.34, shrinking HSACC's lead from 4.53 to 0.21 percentage points. Other datasets and Tables 2–3 retain their results.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(11), mathematical definitions, the linear-kernel assumption, and mutual-information and MMD derivations are unchanged. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and superiority claims concerning hierarchical alignment, dynamic weighting, cooperative completion, and clustering performance.

C2.justification: Interpretations of robustness, component effectiveness, convergence, and representation quality remain unchanged. The conclusion retains the same future-work qualifications concerning complex multimodal data and large-scale applications; the numerical revisions receive no new interpretation.

D1.justification: The architecture dimensions, hardware, PyTorch version, training details, and printed code-access information are unchanged. No implementation or reproducibility explanation is added for the revised scores.

R1.justification: Both contain the same 43 cited works and the same related-work discussion and research positioning. References moving between pages reflect layout changes.

P1.justification: Limited edits update the affiliation and corresponding-author email, correct punctuation, and explicitly reference Figure 2 in the parameter analysis. Section organization and nearly all prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 3 becomes narrower with increased vertical spacing, shifting subsequent text and reference pagination. Table 1 adjusts runner-up underlining to the revised results. All five figures, including the appendix visualization, retain identical image content.

improvement.justification: v4 makes small editorial and layout refinements, but its substantive change is the unexplained replacement of Noisy MNIST scores in Table 1. These markedly alter competitive margins without added validation, protocol explanation, or uncertainty reporting. The PDFs do not establish whether the replacements improve evidential reliability, so a reliable net quality judgment is not possible.
